refreshed_pull_requests.title: API-036: bound and canonicalize pagination cursor decoding
refreshed_pull_requests.body:
## Problem
The API cursor decoder accepted noncanonical base64 spellings of a valid cursor and decoded input without an explicit token-size cap. Session inventory reuses this decoder, so request work must be bounded before decoding.

- Require canonical base64url payload and 43-character SHA-256 signature spellings, rejecting newline and spare-bit aliases.
- Bound the JSON-escaped filter envelope before listing. Reserve 256 encoded position bytes so requests cannot mint cursors the decoder will reject. The largest supported 200-byte listing search still fits even when every search byte requires JSON escaping.
- Add exact-size boundary and allocation measurement coverage; retain key, route, owner and filter binding.

## Provenance and review

refreshed_pull_requests.body:
## Problem

The existing feed helper scans and sorts a supplied snapshot capped at 10,000 rows. It cannot provide database-bounded pagination over large histories. A bounded scan can also advance past unauthorized sources, so a readable signed continuation would disclose private source positions.

## Changes

- Add a module-only SQLite reference store with indexed keyset queries, immutable insertion order, unique source identities and persistent deletion tombstones.
- Add `PageFromStore`: at most 101 candidates per SQL query, 1,000 per request and 100 returned references. An insertion fence excludes later/backdated inserts while current permission checks still apply. Empty/partial pages can carry a continuation.
- Add padded AES-256-GCM v3 cursors that conceal the private frontier, insertion fence and original issue time, with network/viewer/category/preference/key binding and a fixed traversal lifetime.
- Preserve existing valid v2 cursors; harden canonical serialization, typed-nil providers and key ownership.
- Add randomized, adversarial, concurrency, fuzz, 10k/100k real SQLite, query-plan and memory tests. Extend only the existing dedicated feed workflow, explicitly checking out the exact candidate SHA.

refreshed_pull_requests.head: codex/api036-cursor-hardening-20261119
refreshed_pull_requests.body:
## Problem
The API cursor decoder accepted noncanonical base64 spellings of a valid cursor and decoded input without an explicit token-size cap. Session inventory reuses this decoder, so request work must be bounded before decoding.

## Repair
- Reject cursors larger than 4,096 bytes before decoding or MAC work.
- Require canonical base64url payload and 43-character SHA-256 signature spellings, rejecting newline and spare-bit aliases.
- Bound the JSON-escaped filter envelope before listing. Reserve 256 encoded position bytes so requests cannot mint cursors the decoder will reject. The largest supported 200-byte listing search still fits even when every search byte requires JSON escaping.
- Add exact-size boundary and allocation measurement coverage; retain key, route, owner and filter binding.

## Provenance and review
Test-first publication `81f203555e562bc45d86a53341b9b5c44d0b550f` based on PR #90 head `244e1356201e6477eab4694d82947f2058f3b0d8` preserved the old runtime. ## Actual verification
- Fail-before: tests against the actual old API production files rejected the old behavior for payload/signature newlines, signature spare bits, oversized signed payloads and oversized filter envelopes. These were observed test failures, not inferred passes.
- Repaired production-source tests plus existing cursor fuzz seeds: PASS, 0.050 seconds.
- Actual package command: `go test -p 1 -count=1 -run '^TestPagination|^FuzzOpenCursor$' -bench '^BenchmarkPaginationCursorRejectedOversize$' -benchtime=100x -benchmem ./internal/api` PASS, 50.139 seconds. This also includes the existing pagination regression beyond 100 and 2,000 rows.

The existing feed helper scans and sorts a supplied snapshot capped at 10,000 rows. It cannot provide database-bounded pagination over large histories. A bounded scan can advance past unauthorized sources, so a readable signed continuation would disclose private source positions.

- Add a module-only SQLite reference store with indexed keyset queries, immutable ordering/insertion sequence, unique source identities and persistent deletion tombstones.

## Problem and change

Successful Web Push responses returned an error interface holding a nil `*SendError`, so callers treated successful delivery as a failure. - Return a true nil error for successful Web Push responses.
- Validate decimal Retry-After values and clamp seconds before converting to a duration.
- Complete mandatory certificate/name-verified TLS around injected SMTP TCP connections before returning them to go-mail. Its opportunistic state-discovery path then recognizes the already-encrypted connection for authentication; there is no plaintext fallback. The default implicit TLS dialer remains supported.
- Exercise actual STARTTLS/implicit TLS, Web Push encryption/decryption, checked DNS dialing, redirect/private-address refusal, provider classification and redaction, bounded response reads, cancellation, header rejection, and independent concurrent SMTP messages.
